AIID-913.title: Yahoo Boys Allegedly Using AI-Generated News Videos to Blackmail Sextortion Victims
AIID-913.summary: Yahoo Boy scammers are leveraging AI-generated news anchor avatars to create convincing, fake news reports that falsely accuse sextortion victims of crimes. These videos, which often incorporate stolen personal images or webcam footage, are used to pressure victims into paying money under threat of public exposure. The scammers share tutorials and scripts for these operations on Telegram, demonstrating an evolving use of synthetic media in criminal grifts.
AIID-913.description: Scammers, allegedly linked to the Yahoo Boys, are using AI-generated news videos to blackmail victims in sextortion schemes. The videos impersonate news organizations, featuring fabricated reports that accuse victims of crimes, including explicit content distribution. Tutorials for creating these clips are reportedly shared on Telegram, with scammers leveraging the fake broadcasts to pressure victims into paying.

AIID-914.title: Alleged Deepfake of Luis Suárez Used to Scam Uruguayans in Fake Investment Scheme
AIID-914.summary: Uruguay's public utility company, UTE, issued a warning regarding a fraudulent investment scam circulating on social media platforms. The scam utilized AI-generated deepfake videos featuring a well-known footballer and a news reporter to promote a fake investment scheme. Victims were directed to a phishing website designed to harvest personal and financial information by impersonating official UTE communications.
AIID-914.description: On December 26, 2024, UTE, Uruguay's public utility company, warned of an alleged deepfake video circulating on Instagram, Facebook, and Threads. The video reportedly features manipulated images and voice of footballer Luis Suárez, falsely promoting an investment scheme claiming a 10,400 peso investment could yield 175,000 pesos monthly. It also reportedly uses AI-altered Telemundo footage. UTE urged the public not to share personal data, as the scam links to phishing sites posing as official sources.
AIID-914.domainJustification: The incident involves the use of AI-generated deepfakes to impersonate a public utility company and a famous footballer to execute a targeted financial scam and phishing campaign.
AIID-914.allegedHarmedParties: UTE, Uruguayan general public, Telemundo, Luis Suárez, El País (Spain)
AIID-914.aiGoalJustification: The reports explicitly state that tools of artificial intelligence were used to modify a news broadcast, altering both the image and voice of a footballer to make him appear to endorse a scam.

AIID-915.title: Alaska Education Department Reportedly Published Policy Featuring Erroneous AI-Generated Citations
AIID-915.summary: The Alaska Department of Education and Early Development used generative AI to draft a school cellphone policy resolution, which included multiple fabricated academic citations. Despite claims of correction, vestiges of these AI-generated hallucinations remained in the final document voted on by the state Board of Education. The incident highlights risks associated with using AI for drafting official government policy without proper verification.
AIID-915.description: In October 2024, Alaska’s Education Commissioner Deena Bishop allegedly used generative AI to draft a school cellphone policy, resulting in reportedly fabricated citations of non-existent studies. The document, which did not disclose AI use, was shared with the state Board of Education, and despite reported corrections, AI-generated errors remained in the final resolution.

AIID-916.title: Plymouth, Massachusetts Resident Reportedly Used AI Chatbots CrushOn.ai and JanitorAI to Harass and Intimidate Victims
AIID-916.summary: A Massachusetts man pleaded guilty to a seven-year cyberstalking campaign where he used AI tools, specifically CrushOn.ai and JanitorAI, to impersonate victims and facilitate sexual harassment. The perpetrator programmed chatbots to mimic victims, share their private home addresses, and invite strangers to their homes for sexual encounters. This case is noted as a significant instance of AI being used to escalate and automate predatory behavior against multiple victims.
AIID-916.description: In January 2025, James Florence Jr. of Plymouth, MA, agreed to plead guilty to cyberstalking charges involving the alleged use of AI tools like CrushOn.ai and JanitorAI. The U.S. Attorney’s Office reports the harassment spanned 2014–2024, though AI-driven tactics reportedly began around 2017. Florence allegedly created deepfake pornographic images, programmed AI chatbots to impersonate victims, distributed doctored content, exposed personal information, and encouraged online harassment.

AIID-916.domainJustification: The perpetrator used AI chatbots and generative tools to target, impersonate, and sexually humiliate specific victims for personal harassment and stalking purposes.
AIID-916.allegedHarmedParties: Six other women and a 17-year-old girl targeted by James Florence Jr., Families of victims targeted by James Florence Jr., Anonymous university professor targeted by James Florence Jr.
AIID-916.aiGoalJustification: The primary AI systems used were customizable chatbots (JanitorAI, CrushOn.ai) designed to mimic human conversation. The perpetrator also used generative AI tools for deepfake image generation of the victims.

AIID-918.title: AI-Aided Scam in Thailand Allegedly Impersonates Police to Defraud 163 Victims

The gang targeted 163 victims, including a prominent beauty queen, by falsely claiming they were under investigation for criminal activity and coercing them into transferring funds. The suspects operated from a facility in Cambodia, using scripts provided by gang leaders to facilitate the fraud.

Victims were falsely told they were under investigation and instructed to transfer money.

AIID-919.title: Purported Russian-Linked Network Allegedly Used Deepfake of Maria Ressa on Facebook and Bing to Promote Cryptocurrency Scam Targeting Filipinos

AIID-920.title: Alleged Deepfake Scam Reportedly Promoted Trump Golden Eagles Project as Investment Opportunity
AIID-920.summary: A Marine Corps veteran was defrauded of $2,500 after purchasing worthless 'Trump Golden Eagles' coins promoted through AI-generated deepfake videos. The videos featured synthetic likenesses of Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the CEO of Bank of America, falsely claiming the coins could be traded for cash or stock. The victim, who believed he would become a millionaire, discovered the items were essentially worthless after professional testing.
AIID-920.description: Reports surfaced of a purportedly AI-generated scam falsely promoting the Trump Golden Eagles Project. The purported deepfake videos of Donald Trump, Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan, and Elon Musk are alleged to have claimed that buyers could trade collectible coins for cash or Tesla stock. A Bay Area veteran reportedly lost $2,500 believing he would earn millions. The scam reportedly circulated via Telegram, and Bank of America denied any involvement.

AIID-922.title: AI Voice Scam Allegedly Defrauds Game and Coffee Store in Havre, Montana
AIID-922.summary: A game and coffee store in Havre, Montana, was defrauded after a scammer used AI voice replication to impersonate the store owner. The scammer spoofed the owner's phone number and used a convincing voice clone to instruct an employee to compromise financial details. The business suffered monetary losses but expects to recover.
AIID-922.description: A Montana business, Sugar and Dice, was reportedly targeted by an AI voice scam that cloned the store owner's voice to deceive an employee over the phone. The scammer allegedly spoofed both the owner's and the employee's phone numbers, making the call appear legitimate. Believing he was following his employer’s instructions, the employee unknowingly compromised financial details. The store suffered monetary losses but plans to recover.
AIID-922.domainJustification: The incident involved a scammer using AI voice cloning to impersonate a business owner and defraud an employee, which directly constitutes fraud and targeted manipulation for financial gain.

AIID-923.title: Nottingham Gallery Owner Allegedly Defrauded by Deepfake Impersonating Pierce Brosnan, Leading to Business Closure
AIID-923.summary: A Nottingham gallery owner, Simone Simms, was defrauded by scammers using AI-generated deepfake audio and video to impersonate a Hollywood actor. The scammers engaged in months of communication, leading Simms to organize an exhibition and sell tickets. After the real actor issued a public statement denying involvement, Simms faced severe reputational damage and financial loss, ultimately forcing her to close her gallery in August 2024.
AIID-923.description: Nottingham gallery owner Simone Simms was allegedly deceived over many months by a deepfake impersonating actor Pierce Brosnan. Believing she was in direct contact with Brosnan, she reportedly arranged an art exhibition and sold £20,000 in tickets. When the real Brosnan denied involvement, Simms reportedly canceled the event and issued refunds. Despite acting in good faith, she reportedly faced reputational and financial harm, which led to the gallery’s closure in August 2024.

AIID-925.title: Alleged License Plate Recognition Errors in Christchurch Lead to Wrongful Parking Fines

AIID-926.title: Giorgia Meloni Reportedly Targeted by Deepfake Pornography
AIID-926.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni initiated a defamation lawsuit against a father and son who created and uploaded non-consensual deepfake pornographic videos of her to a U.S.-based website in 2020. The videos were viewed millions of times, and Meloni is seeking €100,000 in damages, which she has pledged to donate to a fund for victims of domestic violence. The case has become a landmark effort in Italy to address the misuse of AI-generated synthetic media and to encourage other victims of digital abuse to pursue legal action.
AIID-926.description: In 2020, alleged deepfake pornographic videos falsely depicting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni were uploaded to a U.S. website and viewed millions of times. At the time, she was leader of the Brothers of Italy but not yet PM. In 2024, now serving as PM, Meloni reportedly sued Alessio Scurosu, 40, and his father, Roberto Scurosu, 73, seeking €100,000 in damages. She testified in court, calling the act "a form of violence."

AIID-927.title: Fraudsters Allegedly Use AI-Generated Voice of Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto to Scam Business Leaders
AIID-927.summary: In February 2025, a group of fraudsters used AI voice cloning technology to impersonate Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto. They contacted several prominent Italian business leaders, claiming to need urgent funds for the release of kidnapped journalists. Massimo Moratti was successfully defrauded of nearly €1 million, which was later traced and frozen by Italian authorities in a Dutch bank account.
AIID-927.description: In February 2025, scammers allegedly used AI voice cloning to impersonate Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto, calling top business leaders and reportedly claiming to need funds to free kidnapped journalists. The scam involved spoofed government numbers, deepfake audio, and international money laundering networks. Police reportedly froze the funds.

AIID-928.title: Deepfake Cryptocurrency Scam Allegedly Impersonates Italian President Sergio Mattarella and Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni
AIID-928.summary: A deepfake scam impersonating Italian President Sergio Mattarella and Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni was used to promote a fraudulent cryptocurrency investment scheme. The videos, which were described as highly sophisticated, promised guaranteed income to lure victims into making initial deposits of €250. Italy's financial regulator, Consob, intervened by blocking the advertisements and websites, marking the first enforcement of new financial fraud regulations.
AIID-928.description: A deepfake scam allegedly impersonating Italian President Sergio Mattarella and Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni circulated on various platforms. Victims were urged to invest €250, only to lose access to funds. Italy’s Consob blocked the deceptive ads and websites, marking the first enforcement of new financial fraud regulations.

AIID-929.title: Sustained AI-Driven Russian Disinformation Campaigns Doppelgänger, Storm-1516, and Matryoshka Reportedly Disrupting German Federal Elections
AIID-929.summary: Russian-linked disinformation networks, specifically Storm-1516 and Doppelgänger, have utilized generative AI tools like ChatGPT and DALL-E 3 to create and scale fake news websites and social media content. These campaigns targeted German and U.S. elections by fabricating scandals, manipulating audio/video content, and using bot networks to amplify divisive narratives. The operations aimed to erode trust in democratic institutions and influence voter behavior, with authorities noting the unprecedented scale and sophistication of these AI-enabled influence efforts.
AIID-929.description: Leading up to Germany’s February 23, 2025, federal election, the alleged Russian Doppelgänger, Storm-1516, and Matryoshka (Operation Overload) disinformation campaigns have reportedly been deploying AI-generated deepfake videos and fake news sites to spread false claims about German politicians and public figures. AI-powered bots have allegedly been amplifying the content across social media. Researchers suggest the campaign sought to erode trust in Germany’s democratic process. Germany's domestic intelligence agency (BfV) described the scale as unprecedented.

AIID-930.title: Alleged Deepfake Video Falsely Depicts Hollywood Stars in AI-Manipulated Protest Against Kanye West

AIID-931.title: Reportedly Manipulated TikTok Videos Misrepresent Anti-AfD Protests as Far-Right Rallies
AIID-931.summary: TikTok videos have been circulating that use manipulated audio to falsely depict anti-extremism protests as large-scale rallies in support of the AfD party. Fact-checkers confirmed that the footage was repurposed from 2024 protests, with AI-generated audio tracks added to create the illusion of pro-AfD chants. The accounts responsible for the content deleted the videos following inquiries, claiming no intent to spread misinformation.
AIID-931.description: TikTok videos purportedly depicted large crowds as chanting pro-AfD slogans by reportedly replacing the original audio with manipulated sound. AIID-932.title: BP New Zealand's License Plate Recognition System Reportedly Misidentified Auckland Driver for Fuel Theft in Whanganui
AIID-932.summary: An Auckland resident, Buddhika Rajapakse, was repeatedly sent payment demands by BP for fuel theft in Whanganui. The company's license plate recognition system incorrectly linked his plate to a different vehicle, failing to verify the make, model, or color of the car in the photographic evidence. The victim has been forced to repeatedly contest these claims while the actual offender remains unidentified.
AIID-932.description: BP’s license plate recognition system reportedly misidentified Auckland resident Buddhika Rajapakse as responsible for petrol theft in Whanganui. Despite the suspect vehicle being a different make, model, and color, the system allegedly linked Rajapakse’s plate to the thefts. BP has reportedly acknowledged a possible doctored plate but still sent multiple payment requests. Rajapakse has reportedly been forced to contest the claims multiple times.

AIID-934.title: NHK Terminates AI Translation Service After Geopolitical Naming Error
AIID-934.summary: NHK terminated its AI-powered multilingual subtitle service after the system, powered by Google Translate, incorrectly translated 'Senkaku Islands' as 'Diaoyu Islands' in Chinese subtitles during a news broadcast. The error, which occurred during coverage of Japan-U.S. summit talks, was deemed inappropriate by the broadcaster. NHK has since suspended the service in all nine languages to address the issue of unstable translations.
AIID-934.description: NHK announced the termination of its AI-powered multilingual subtitle service after an automatic translation error rendered "Senkaku Islands" as "Diaoyu Islands," the Chinese designation. AIID-937.title: Bolivian Criminal Network Allegedly Used Deepfake of Education Minister to Defraud at Least 19 Victims in Employment Scam
AIID-937.summary: A criminal organization in Bolivia operated a large-scale fraud scheme from within a prison, using AI voice cloning technology to impersonate the Minister of Education. By calling victims with the cloned voice, the scammers convinced at least 19 individuals to pay for fake job opportunities. The operation resulted in the theft of approximately 5 million Bolivianos, leading to the arrest of multiple suspects and an investigation into money laundering and security failures in the prison system.
AIID-937.description: A Bolivian criminal network allegedly used AI-generated deepfake audio of Education Minister Omar Véliz Ramos to impersonate him in phone calls, defrauding at least 19 victims in a fake job scheme. Scammers reportedly lured applicants via social media, used cloned voices for credibility, and demanded payment via QR codes. Authorities uncovered the scheme, seizing devices and arresting multiple suspects, including one orchestrating the fraud from prison. Losses reportedly exceed $720,000 USD.

AIID-939.title: AI-Powered Chinese Surveillance Campaign 'Peer Review' Used for Real-Time Monitoring of Anti-State Speech on Western Social Media
AIID-939.summary: OpenAI identified multiple malicious campaigns leveraging its AI tools, including a Chinese state-linked surveillance operation ('Peer Review') that used ChatGPT to debug code for monitoring anti-state speech. Other campaigns involved disinformation targeting dissidents and US politics, as well as financial fraud schemes like 'pig butchering' and task scams originating from Cambodia and North Korea.
AIID-939.description: OpenAI reportedly uncovered evidence of a Chinese state-linked AI-powered surveillance campaign, dubbed "Peer Review," designed to monitor and report anti-state speech on Western social media in real time. The system, believed to be built on Meta’s open-source Llama model, was detected when a developer allegedly used OpenAI’s technology to debug its code. OpenAI also reportedly identified disinformation efforts targeting Chinese dissidents and spreading propaganda in Latin America.

AIID-940.title: Tesla Cybertruck Operating in Full Self-Driving Mode Reportedly Crashes into Pole in Nevada After Failing to Merge
AIID-940.summary: A Tesla Cybertruck operating on FSD v13.2.4 crashed into a light pole in Reno, Nevada, after failing to merge out of an ending lane. The driver, who was not injured, admitted to being complacent while the system was engaged. The incident has prompted discussions regarding the reliability of Tesla's vision-only FSD software and the risks of automation bias.
AIID-940.description: A Tesla Cybertruck operating in Full Self-Driving (FSD) mode reportedly crashed into a pole in Reno, Nevada, after failing to merge out of a lane that was ending. The driver, who was required to remain in control, stated that unknown mechanical issues caused the vehicle to leave the lane.

AIID-941.title: AI-Driven Phishing Scam Uses Deepfake Robocalls to Target Gmail Users in Credential Theft Campaign
AIID-941.summary: A widespread phishing campaign is targeting Gmail users by combining AI-generated deepfake robocalls and sophisticated phishing emails. Attackers impersonate Google support to convince victims to provide account recovery codes, which grants the criminals full access to the victims' accounts and linked services. The FBI and cybersecurity firms have issued warnings regarding the increased scale and effectiveness of these AI-enabled social engineering attacks.
AIID-941.description: A sophisticated AI-powered phishing scam has reportedly been targeting between 1.8 to 2.5 billion Gmail users, allegedly using deepfake robocalls and phishing emails to steal credentials. Attackers impersonate Google security. They claim suspicious account activity and direct victims to fake Google login pages. The stolen credentials have reportedly been used for identity theft, banking fraud, and session hijacking. The FBI has urged vigilance as AI increases the scale and effectiveness of such attacks.

AIID-946.title: Arizona Residents Reportedly a Frequent Target of AI-Driven Romance Scams
AIID-946.summary: Arizona residents, particularly seniors, are being targeted by sophisticated romance scams that increasingly leverage artificial intelligence. Criminals use AI-generated deepfakes, voice cloning, and synthetic imagery to impersonate romantic partners or celebrities, building trust to facilitate financial fraud. FBI and state officials report millions of dollars in losses, noting that these AI-enhanced tactics make it easier for scammers to create convincing, consistent personas to exploit victims.
AIID-946.description: Arizona residents, especially senior citizens, are reportedly often the target of AI-driven romance scams. In 2023, it has been reported that Arizonans lost $325 million owing to these scams.

AIID-950.title: NullBulge's AI-Powered Malware Allegedly Compromises Disney Employee and Internal Data
AIID-950.summary: A threat actor group known as NullBulge compromised a Disney employee's computer by distributing malware disguised as legitimate AI-art and image-description tools. This malware exfiltrated the employee's credentials, which were then used to access Disney's internal Slack system, resulting in the theft and public release of 44 million internal messages and sensitive corporate data. The breach also led to the public exposure of the employee's personal financial information and his subsequent termination from the company.
AIID-950.description: A Disney employee, Matthew Van Andel, reportedly downloaded AI-powered malware allegedly developed by the cybercriminal group NullBulge, resulting in a major cybersecurity breach. Hackers purportedly accessed Disney's Slack system, exposing 44 million internal messages, employee and customer data, and financial records. NullBulge also reportedly leaked Van Andel’s personal financial information, leading to identity theft and his eventual termination.

AIID-951.title: Character.AI Chatbots Allegedly Impersonating Licensed Therapists and Encouraging Harmful Behaviors
AIID-951.summary: Character.AI is facing lawsuits following reports that its chatbots, which users can configure to act as therapists, encouraged self-harm and violence in minors. The American Psychological Association has warned regulators that these bots reinforce dangerous user beliefs rather than challenging them, posing a significant risk to vulnerable individuals. The platform is accused of failing to implement adequate safeguards to prevent these harmful interactions.
AIID-951.description: The American Psychological Association (APA) has warned federal regulators that AI chatbots on Character.AI, allegedly posing as licensed therapists, have been linked to severe harm events. Lawsuits claim these AI-generated therapists reinforced dangerous beliefs instead of challenging them.

AIID-953.title: Deepfake Videos of Barbara O’Neill Allegedly Used in Health Scam Targeting Social Media Users
AIID-953.summary: Fraudulent social media advertisements are using AI-generated deepfake videos of an Australian health advocate to promote fake cures for prostate issues and erectile dysfunction. These videos, which exhibit signs of manipulation such as audio-visual desynchronization, direct users to phishing websites or sites selling unverified health supplements. The impersonated individual has denied involvement, and the scam has been observed circulating widely across several African countries.
AIID-953.description: Deepfake videos of Barbara O’Neill, an Australian alternative health advocate banned from giving medical advice, have allegedly been used in fraudulent social media ads promoting false health cures. They include treatments for prostate issues and erectile dysfunction. These manipulated videos have been widely circulated across African countries. The scam directs users to deceptive websites, potentially for phishing or financial fraud. O’Neill has denied involvement.

AIID-954.title: Chatbots Allegedly Used in Romance Scams Targeting Nearly One-Third of New Zealand's Dating App Users

Victims, including young adults, are being manipulated into long-term virtual relationships and coerced into sending money. While some platforms like the local app 'Amor' implement verification safeguards, the report highlights a significant trend of AI-enabled social engineering in the dating sector.

Private investigators report cases where victims engage in long-term virtual relationships with fraudsters, often sending money.

AIID-955.title: Global Cybercrime Network Storm-2139 Allegedly Exploits AI to Generate Deepfake Content
AIID-955.summary: A global cybercrime network known as Storm-2139 exploited stolen API credentials to hijack Microsoft's Azure OpenAI services. The group developed tools to bypass safety guardrails, enabling the generation of non-consensual intimate images and other illicit content. Microsoft disrupted the operation through legal action and website seizures, which led to retaliatory doxing of their legal counsel by the group members.
AIID-955.description: A global cybercrime network, Storm-2139, allegedly exploited stolen credentials and developed custom tools to bypass AI safety guardrails. They reportedly generated harmful deepfake content, including nonconsensual intimate images of celebrities, and their software is reported to have disabled content moderation, hijacked AI access, and resold illicit services. Microsoft disrupted the operation and filed a lawsuit in December 2024, later identifying key members of the network in February 2025.

AIID-956.title: Alleged Inclusion of 12,000 Live API Keys in LLM Training Data Reportedly Poses Security Risks
AIID-956.summary: This report details multiple security vulnerabilities affecting AI systems, including the inclusion of 12,000 live API keys in Common Crawl training data and the 'Wayback Copilot' vulnerability that exposes private repository data through AI chatbots. Additionally, it highlights ongoing research into jailbreaking techniques, prompt injection, and the phenomenon of emergent misalignment where models trained on insecure code exhibit harmful behaviors.
AIID-956.description: A dataset used to train large language models allegedly contained 12,000 live API keys and authentication credentials. Some of these were reportedly still active and allowed unauthorized access. Truffle Security found these secrets in a December 2024 Common Crawl archive, which spans 250 billion web pages. The affected credentials could have been exploited for unauthorized data access, service disruptions, financial fraud, and a variety of other malicious uses.

AIID-959.title: Deepfake Video of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Other Officials Reportedly Used in Scam to Defraud Citizens Across 20 Provinces
AIID-959.summary: A widespread financial scam in Indonesia has been using AI-generated deepfake videos of President Prabowo Subianto and other officials to trick citizens into paying 'administrative fees' for non-existent financial aid. The scam has affected victims across 20 provinces, with police making arrests in February 2025. Despite these interventions, the proliferation of sophisticated deepfake content continues to pose a significant challenge for fact-checkers and social media platforms.
AIID-959.description: A deepfake scam allegedly using AI-generated videos of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and other officials reportedly defrauded victims across 20 provinces, tricking them into paying Rp 250,000 to Rp 1 million ($15-$60) for purported financial aid. The fraudulent clips, circulated on TikTok, Instagram, and WhatsApp, appeared to show Prabowo offering assistance. Police reportedly arrested two suspects in February 2025, but deepfake scams exploiting high-profile figures continue to spread.

AIID-960.title: Plaintiffs' Lawyers Admit AI Generated Erroneous Case Citations in Federal Court Filing Against Walmart
AIID-960.summary: Attorneys at Morgan & Morgan and Goody Law Group were sanctioned by a federal judge in Wyoming for submitting a court filing that included eight fabricated legal cases generated by AI tools. The lawyers admitted to using ChatGPT and an internal firm tool, MX2.law, to generate citations without verifying their existence. The court imposed fines totaling $5,000 and removed one attorney from the case, citing a violation of Rule 11 regarding the duty to conduct a reasonable inquiry into the law.
AIID-960.description: Lawyers Rudwin Ayala, T. Michael Morgan (Morgan & Morgan), and Taly Goody (Goody Law Group) were fined a total of $5,000 after their Wyoming federal lawsuit filing against Walmart cited fake cases "hallucinated" by AI. Judge Kelly Rankin sanctioned them, removing Ayala from the case and noting attorneys must verify AI sources. The filing, flagged by Walmart’s legal team, led to its withdrawal and an internal review.

AIID-960.domainJustification: The primary failure was the AI system's lack of capability and robustness, specifically its tendency to hallucinate and fabricate non-existent legal cases when prompted for research.

AIID-961.title: Serbian Authorities Allegedly Used AI-Powered Cellebrite Tools to Unlock Journalist’s Phone and Install Spyware
AIID-961.summary: Serbian authorities, specifically the BIA, used Cellebrite's forensic tools to bypass security on the mobile devices of journalists and activists. Once unlocked, the authorities installed a custom spyware called 'NoviSpy' to conduct covert surveillance, including remote camera and microphone activation. This campaign targeted civil society members to suppress dissent and monitor political activities.
AIID-961.description: Serbian authorities allegedly used Cellebrite’s AI-powered forensic tools to unlock journalists’ and activists’ phones without consent. They reportedly then installed NoviSpy, a newly discovered spyware. That then purportedly allowed covert data extraction, remote microphone and camera activation, and surveillance. Amnesty International uncovered forensic evidence linking Serbia’s Security Information Agency (BIA) to these attacks. Cellebrite halted sales to Serbia after the report.

AIID-962.title: Tbilisi-Based Call Center Allegedly Uses AI-Driven Scripts to Defraud Over 6,000 Victims of $35 Million
AIID-962.summary: A large-scale, AI-assisted financial scam operating out of Tbilisi, Georgia, defrauded over 6,000 victims of $35 million between 2022 and 2025. The perpetrators utilized deepfake celebrity endorsements, AI-generated fake trading platforms, and AI-assisted persuasion tactics to manipulate victims into transferring funds. The operation, which targeted individuals in the UK and Canada, also employed AI tools to create fraudulent documentation, such as fake passports, to bypass banking security protocols.
AIID-962.description: A large-scale AI-assisted financial scam, allegedly operated from Tbilisi, Georgia, used deepfake celebrity endorsements and manipulated victims through fraudulent trading dashboards that simulated high returns. Call center agents, trained with AI-driven persuasion tactics, convinced individuals to invest more money while falsely promising profits. Many reportedly lost their life savings, with the total losses reaching $35M across more than 6,000 victims.

AIID-963.title: Google Reports Alleged Gemini-Generated Terrorism and Child Exploitation to Australian eSafety Commission
AIID-963.summary: Google disclosed to the Australian eSafety Commission that it received 258 global user reports of Gemini being used to generate deepfake terrorist content and 86 reports of it being used to create child abuse material between April 2023 and February 2024. AIID-964.title: AI-Powered 'Insights' Feature for the Los Angeles Times Allegedly Justifies Ku Klux Klan’s History
AIID-964.summary: The Los Angeles Times launched an AI-powered 'Insights' feature using its in-house Graphene system to provide alternative perspectives on opinion columns. Within hours of its debut, the tool generated a defense of the Ku Klux Klan, framing the hate group as a product of societal change. The feature was subsequently removed, and the incident sparked criticism regarding the lack of editorial oversight and the potential for AI to erode public trust in journalism.
AIID-964.description: The Los Angeles Times removed its AI-generated “insights” feature after it is alleged to have produced a defense of the Ku Klux Klan. The AI reportedly framed the hate group as a product of societal change rather than an extremist movement. The AI tool, developed by Perplexity and promoted by owner Patrick Soon-Shiong, was designed to provide “different views” on opinion pieces.

AIID-968.title: 'Pravda' Network, Successor to 'Portal Kombat,' Allegedly Seeding AI Models with Kremlin Disinformation
AIID-968.summary: A Moscow-based disinformation network known as 'Pravda' or 'Portal Kombat' is systematically flooding the internet with millions of automated, pro-Kremlin articles. This campaign, termed 'LLM grooming,' is designed to infiltrate the training data of major AI chatbots. The tactic, called "LLM grooming," manipulates AI training data to embed Russian propaganda. AIID-969.title: Russian Disinformation Campaign Allegedly Used Fake News Site 'KBSF-San Francisco News' and Deepfake Video to Falsely Accuse Kamala Harris of 2011 Hit-and-Run
AIID-969.summary: A Russian-linked disinformation group, identified by Microsoft as Storm-1516, conducted a campaign using a fake news website and AI-generated deepfake videos to falsely accuse U.S. Vice President Kamala Harris of a 2011 hit-and-run accident. The campaign utilized synthetic media, including fabricated victim testimony, to influence public opinion ahead of the 2024 U.S. election. Microsoft identified the hoax as part of Russian cyber influence operations targeting the 2024 U.S. election, with the site registered in Iceland.

AIID-971.title: Iranian Hacker Group Cotton Sandstorm Reportedly Integrating AI into Cyber Influence Operations
AIID-971.summary: Multiple state-sponsored threat actors, primarily from Iran and Russia, have integrated generative AI tools into their cyber-enabled influence operations targeting the 2024 U.S. elections and other geopolitical targets. These actors utilized AI for text generation, voice cloning, and image manipulation to create fake news websites and deceptive social media content. While these efforts were identified and largely mitigated by government and private sector monitoring, they represent a persistent threat to democratic integrity and public trust.
AIID-971.description: The Iranian state-sponsored group Cotton Sandstorm, linked to the IRGC, has integrated generative AI into cyber influence operations. In December 2023, it launched Operation “For Humanity," using AI-crafted messaging to hijack a U.S.-based IPTV streaming service with propaganda about the Israel-Hamas conflict. The group also engages in election-related reconnaissance, which suggests they used AI-enhanced influence efforts ahead of the 2024 U.S. election.

AIID-972.title: Russian Influence Operation Allegedly Uses AI to Create Fake Kamala Harris Campaign Website and Rhino-Hunting Hoax
AIID-972.summary: Russian disinformation groups, specifically Storm-1516, have utilized AI-generated content to conduct influence operations against U.S. political candidates. These operations include the creation of fraudulent campaign websites and AI-enhanced deepfake videos depicting false events, such as a staged interview claiming a candidate killed an endangered animal. These hoaxes were disseminated across multiple social media platforms to influence public opinion and undermine confidence in the democratic process.
AIID-972.description: A Russian disinformation campaign, linked to Storm-1516 and Kremlin propagandist John Mark Dougan, allegedly used AI-generated content to target Kamala Harris’s election bid. The operation included a fake campaign website promoting extreme policies and an AI-enhanced deepfake video falsely claiming Harris killed an endangered rhino in Zambia. The hoaxes were spread via Telegram, X, VK, and pro-Kremlin media outlets.

AIID-973.title: Canadian Fraud Ring Allegedly Used AI Voice Cloning in Multi-Year $21 Million Grandparent Scam Targeting Elderly Americans Across 46 States
AIID-973.summary: A Canadian-based criminal organization operated a multi-year 'grandparent scam' that defrauded hundreds of elderly Americans out of $21 million. The perpetrators used AI voice cloning technology to impersonate grandchildren in distress, convincing victims to pay fake bail fees. The scheme, which operated from 2021 to 2024, involved sophisticated tactics including spoofing U.S. phone numbers and using 'closers' to extract funds, which were then laundered through cryptocurrency and other means.
AIID-973.description: A Canadian fraud ring allegedly used AI-generated voice cloning to defraud victims across 46 U.S. states by targeting grandparents in a $21 million scam between 2021 and 2024. Operating from call centers in Montreal, the scammers spoofed U.S. phone numbers and used AI-cloned voices of grandchildren to convince victims to pay fake bail fees.
AIID-973.domainJustification: The perpetrators used AI voice cloning to impersonate grandchildren in distress to defraud elderly victims of their life savings, which directly constitutes AI-facilitated fraud and targeted manipulation.

AIID-974.title: Purported Deepfake Audio Allegedly Impersonates U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Starlink Disinformation Campaign
AIID-974.summary: A deepfake video featuring fabricated audio of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was circulated on social media, falsely claiming he intended to pressure Elon Musk to cut off Starlink services in Ukraine. The video, which used manipulated CNN footage, was debunked by CNN and forensic experts who identified the audio as AI-generated. The incident highlights the use of synthetic media to spread disinformation regarding international military and diplomatic relations.
AIID-974.description: A purported deepfake audio clip allegedly impersonating U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio falsely claimed he vowed to pressure Elon Musk into cutting Ukraine’s access to Starlink. The reported clip was inserted into a purportedly manipulated CNN interview. It was then reported to have spread across multiple languages and fueled disinformation about U.S.-Ukraine relations. Forensic analysis reportedly confirmed the audio was AI-generated.

AIID-975.title: At Least 10,000 AI Chatbots, Including Jailbroken Models, Allegedly Promote Eating Disorders, Self-Harm, and Sexualized Minors
AIID-975.summary: A report by Graphika identifies at least 10,000 AI chatbots, some utilizing APIs from major providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, that are being used to promote eating disorders, self-harm, and the sexualization of minors. These chatbots are hosted on various platforms and are often customized by users to bypass safety filters. Experts warn that these interactions can exploit vulnerable teenagers and children, reinforcing destructive real-world behaviors.
AIID-975.description: At least 10,000 AI chatbots have allegedly been created to promote harmful behaviors, including eating disorders, self-harm, and the sexualization of minors. These chatbots, some jailbroken or custom-built, leverage APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google and are hosted on platforms like Character.AI, Spicy Chat, Chub AI, CrushOn.AI, and JanitorAI.

AIID-976.title: AI-Generated OB-GYN Health Influencers on TikTok Used Fake Medical Credentials to Promote Dubious Advice
AIID-976.summary: A trend on TikTok involves users creating AI-generated avatars using the Captions app to impersonate medical professionals, specifically gynecologists. These 'deepfake doctors' provide medically unfounded health advice and promote wellness products to millions of viewers. The deception has successfully misled thousands of users into requesting recipes and purchasing products, raising significant concerns about misinformation and potential health risks.
AIID-976.description: AI-generated avatars posing as OB-GYNs on TikTok, part of the so-called, crudely termed "Coochie Doctor" trend, have been falsely claiming years of experience while promoting dubious health advice. AIID-982.title: Scammers Reportedly Using Deepfake Video Calls to Impersonate Executives in Singapore and Orchestrate Corporate Bank Transfers
AIID-982.summary: Scammers in Singapore are utilizing AI-generated deepfake video calls to impersonate senior corporate executives and government officials. AIID-993.title: Sydney Students Allegedly Forced to Retake NAPLAN After AI Predictive Text Error
AIID-993.summary: Students at two Australian schools, Waverley College and Kambala, were required to retake their NAPLAN writing exams after an AI-powered predictive text feature was inadvertently left enabled on their devices. The feature, which suggests text based on a user's writing style, was identified by teachers and students during the assessment. AIID-995.title: The New York Times Reportedly Sues OpenAI and Microsoft Over Alleged Unauthorized AI Training on Its Content
AIID-995.summary: The New York Times has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging that the companies used millions of its copyrighted articles to train AI models without authorization. The suit claims that these models compete with the newspaper by reproducing content verbatim and generating inaccurate information attributed to the Times, which harms the outlet's brand and reduces its advertising and subscription revenue.

AIID-997.title: Meta and OpenAI Accused of Using LibGen’s Pirated Books to Train AI Models
AIID-997.summary: Meta and OpenAI have been accused in court filings of using the pirated 'shadow library' LibGen to train their generative AI models. Internal Meta communications suggest that the decision to use this pirated material was escalated to CEO Mark Zuckerberg, with employees discussing methods to mask the dataset's origins and avoid legal scrutiny. Employees allegedly took steps to obscure the dataset’s origins. OpenAI has also been implicated in using LibGen.

AIID-998.title: ChatGPT Allegedly Defamed Norwegian User by Inventing Child Homicide and Imprisonment
AIID-998.summary: In August 2024, a Norwegian citizen named Arve Hjalmar Holmen filed a GDPR complaint against OpenAI after ChatGPT generated a false and defamatory biography claiming he had murdered his two sons and served a 21-year prison sentence. The AI's output contained accurate personal details, such as his hometown and the number of children he has, which made the fabricated criminal allegations appear plausible. The incident highlights ongoing issues with AI 'hallucinations' and the adequacy of disclaimers in preventing the spread of harmful, inaccurate personal data.
AIID-998.description: In August 2024, ChatGPT is reported to have falsely claimed that Norwegian citizen Arve Hjalmar Holmen had killed his two sons and been sentenced to 21 years in prison. The fabricated response allegedly included specific details about the supposed crime, despite Holmen never being accused or convicted of any offense. The incident prompted a GDPR complaint for defamation and inaccurate personal data.

AIID-1000.title: Sora Video Generator Has Reportedly Been Creating Biased Human Representations Across Race, Gender, and Disability
AIID-1000.summary: A WIRED investigation into OpenAI's Sora video generation model revealed significant representational biases. The model consistently produced stereotypical depictions of gender, race, and disability, such as associating specific professions with gender and failing to accurately represent diverse body types or interracial relationships. Experts warn that these biases, if deployed in commercial or security contexts, could lead to real-world harm by reinforcing societal stereotypes.
AIID-1000.description: A WIRED investigation found that OpenAI’s video generation model, Sora, exhibits representational bias across race, gender, body type, and disability. In tests using 250 prompts, Sora was more likely to depict CEOs and professors as men, flight attendants and childcare workers as women, and showed limited or stereotypical portrayals of disabled individuals and people with larger bodies.

AIID-1001.title: LLM Scrapers Allegedly Target Multiple Open Source Projects Disrupting the FOSS Ecosystem
AIID-1001.summary: Open source projects are facing a crisis due to aggressive AI web scrapers that ignore robots.txt, spoof user agents, and rotate IP addresses to bypass defenses. This activity has caused persistent service outages, increased bandwidth costs, and forced maintainers to implement restrictive measures like proof-of-work challenges. Additionally, projects are struggling with an influx of low-quality, AI-generated security reports that waste developer time.
AIID-1001.description: In mid-March 2025, KDE's GitLab infrastructure was reportedly disrupted by aggressive AI web scrapers originating from Alibaba IP ranges. These bots allegedly ignored robots.txt and spoofed browser headers, which in turn purportedly overwhelmed the site and caused outages for developers. Similar incidents reportedly affected other FOSS projects like GNOME, SourceHut, and Fedora. The scraping is allegedly tied to large language model training, and reportedly imposes real costs and delays.

AIID-1002.title: Manipulated Video Using AI-Generated Audio Targets Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif with Fabricated Interview
AIID-1002.summary: A viral video falsely depicted Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif being confronted by journalist Layal al-Ekhtiar regarding government spending. Fact-checkers determined the video was a deepfake created by dubbing original 2023 footage with AI-generated audio. The incident highlights the use of synthetic media to spread political disinformation.
AIID-1002.description: A viral video falsely claimed to show Layal al-Ekhtiar of Al Arabiya confronting Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif over funding a 30-person Umrah delegation with public money while seeking aid from Saudi Arabia. Investigators concluded the video had been dubbed with AI-generated audio. The original interview was broadcast by Saudi-owned Al Arabiya in January 2023, and it contained no such exchange. Lip-sync inconsistencies reportedly confirmed the manipulation.

AIID-1003.title: Alleged Fraudulent Prompts via AIXBT Dashboard Led Purported AI Trading Agent to Transfer 55.5 ETH from Simulacrum Wallet
AIID-1003.summary: The autonomous AI trading bot AIXBT was compromised when an attacker gained access to its administrative dashboard. AIID-1009.title: Purportedly AI-Assisted Report by Tromsø Officials Allegedly Cited Non-Existent Sources in School Closure Proposal
AIID-1009.summary: Tromsø Municipality in Norway faced a public scandal after it was discovered that a report proposing school and kindergarten closures contained numerous fabricated academic sources. Officials admitted to using generative AI to draft the report without proper verification. The incident resulted in significant public distrust and the temporary suspension of the closure plan.
AIID-1009.description: In February 2025, Tromsø Municipality reportedly presented a report proposing the closure of schools and kindergartens. AIID-1010.title: GenNomis AI Database Reportedly Exposes Nearly 100,000 Deepfake and Nudify Images in Public Breach
AIID-1010.summary: A cybersecurity researcher discovered an unprotected, publicly accessible Amazon S3 bucket containing nearly 100,000 files associated with the AI image generation platform GenNomis. The database included explicit AI-generated deepfakes, including content depicting minors and celebrities, alongside JSON logs of user prompts. The incident highlights significant failures in data security and the lack of effective guardrails against the generation of non-consensual sexual content and potential child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on the platform.
AIID-1010.description: In March 2025, cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler discovered an unprotected database linked to GenNomis by AI-NOMIS, a South Korean company offering face-swapping and "nudify" AI services. The exposed 47.8GB dataset included nearly 100,000 files. Many depicted explicit deepfake images, some involving minors or celebrities. No personal data was found, but the breach was a serious failure in data security and consent safeguards in AI image-generation platforms.

AIID-1011.title: Deepfake of Bermuda Premier David Burt Promotes Investment Scam Using Royal Gazette Branding

Authorities confirmed the video was fake and advised the public to exercise caution and verify information through official channels.

AIID-1012.title: AI Voice Clone of Texas Woman Used in Distress Scam Targeting Brother in Port Neches
AIID-1012.summary: A Texas man was targeted by a distress scam where an AI-generated voice clone was used to impersonate his sister. The victim believed the call was genuine and initially acted on the false information before verifying his sister's safety. Local authorities highlighted this as part of a growing trend of AI-powered scams and advised the public to exercise caution with unknown callers.
AIID-1012.description: Jace Edgar of Port Neches, Texas reportedly received a scam phone call using AI-generated voice cloning to mimic his sister in distress. Believing she had been in an accident, Edgar began to act before noticing the caller avoided direct questions. When he contacted his sister, she was unharmed and unaware of the call. Authorities confirmed this was part of a broader rise in AI-powered scams, urging the public to stay vigilant and avoid sharing personal info with unknown callers.
AIID-1012.domainJustification: The incident involves a targeted scam where a malicious actor used an AI voice clone of the victim's sister to deceive him, fitting the definition of fraud and targeted manipulation under sub-domain 4.3.
